mainTopic: Forbidden wine (יין נסך) mixed into vinegar, and whether smell alone counts as forbidden benefit (בת תיהא)
overview: This amud finishes the argument between אביי and רבא about forbidden wine that fell into a barrel of vinegar. אביי says the wine already smells like vinegar, so it counts as vinegar mixed with vinegar and forbids במשהו. רבא says taste decides, so it is still wine mixed with vinegar and forbids only בנותן טעם. The גמרא then brings a second argument between them, about a ישראל smelling a גוי's wine through the hole of the barrel (בת תיהא). אביי forbids this because smell counts, and רבא permits it because smell is nothing. רבא brings a proof from a משנה about bread baked in an oven heated with תרומה cumin, and אביי answers that there the forbidden cumin was already burned up. רב מרי then says their argument matches an argument of תנאים about hot bread placed on a barrel of תרומה wine. אביי begins to answer by quoting ריש לקיש, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי's reasoning: the wine counts as vinegar
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains why forbidden wine that fell into vinegar forbids the mixture by any amount. The wine already smells like vinegar, so it counts as vinegar, and same-type mixtures are forbidden במשהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A liquid that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine counts as vinegar. So this is a case of one kind mixed with its own kind, and any kind mixed with its own kind makes the mixture forbidden by even a tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's explanation of why forbidden wine that fell into vinegar forbids the whole barrel even in a tiny amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says that what a liquid smells like decides what it is. Once the wine smells like vinegar, it counts as vinegar mixed into vinegar, which is מין במינו. A same-type mixture is not cancelled by a larger amount, so it is forbidden במשהו.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind mixed with its own kind
by any amount, even a tiny bit

phrases.english: Its smell is vinegar and its taste is wine: it counts as vinegar,
phrases.notes: This is still אביי speaking. He is talking about the forbidden wine that fell into the vinegar barrel.

phrases.english: and so it becomes a kind mixed with its own kind,
and any kind mixed with its own kind forbids by any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's ruling from before this section, explaining his reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine that smells like vinegar counts as vinegar, so it is מין במינו and forbids במשהו.

steps.title: רבא's view: the wine still counts as wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees. He says the mixture is forbidden only בנותן טעם, because a liquid that tastes like wine still counts as wine, so wine in vinegar is a mix of different kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: it is forbidden only if the wine adds taste. Something that smells like vinegar but tastes like wine counts as wine. So this is one kind mixed with a different kind, and any kind mixed with a different kind is forbidden only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with אביי and says the barrel is forbidden only if the forbidden wine can actually be tasted in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the facts: smell of vinegar, taste of wine. They disagree about which one decides what the liquid is. For רבא, taste decides, so the wine is still wine, and wine in vinegar is מין בשאינו מינו, which follows the rule of נותן טעם.

keyTerms.meaning: only when it gives noticeable taste
a kind mixed with a different kind

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: smell decides, so it is vinegar in vinegar and forbidden במשהו. רבא: taste decides, so it is wine in vinegar and forbidden only בנותן טעם.
steps.confusionAlert: They do not argue about the rules of mixtures. Both agree same-kind is במשהו and different-kind is בנותן טעם. They only argue about whether this wine counts as vinegar or as wine.

phrases.english: Rava says: it is forbidden only when it gives taste,
since its smell is vinegar and its taste is wine, it counts as wine,
and so it becomes a kind mixed with a different kind,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.english: and any kind mixed with a different kind forbids only when it gives taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to אביי's reasoning in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taste decides what the liquid is, so it is מין בשאינו מינו and forbids only בנותן טעם.

steps.title: Smelling wine through the barrel's hole
steps.stepSummary: A new case: smelling wine through the hole of a barrel (בת תיהא). A גוי smelling a ישראל's wine is fine. אביי and רבא argue about a ישראל smelling a גוי's wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the hole of a barrel: if a non-Jew smells a Jew's wine through it, that is fine. If a Jew smells a non-Jew's wine through it, אביי says it is forbidden and רבא says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between אביי and רבא, this time about smelling wine through the hole of a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גוי smells a ישראל's wine, he does not touch it, so the wine does not become forbidden. The question is the other way around: may a ישראל get pleasure from the smell of a גוי's wine, which is forbidden for benefit?

keyTerms.meaning: the hole in a wine barrel through which you can smell the wine

phrases.english: This hole of the barrel:
a non-Jew smelling a Jew's wine is fine,
phrases.notes: Literally just "a non-Jew with a Jew's." The word "smelling" is understood from the case.

phrases.english: a Jew smelling a non-Jew's wine:
Abaye says: forbidden,
Rava says: permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about smell, related to the smell discussion in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי smelling a ישראל's wine is permitted. On a ישראל smelling a גוי's wine, אביי forbids and רבא permits.

steps.title: The reasons: does smell count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both views. אביי holds that smell is something real. רבא holds that smell is nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says it is forbidden because smell is something real. רבא says it is permitted because smell is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the argument about smelling a גוי's wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument depends on one question: is enjoying a smell a real kind of benefit? If it is (אביי), smelling forbidden wine is forbidden benefit. If it is not (רבא), nothing forbidden happened.

keyTerms.meaning: it is something real, it counts
it is nothing, it does not count

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: ריחא מילתא היא, smell counts. רבא: ריחא לאו מילתא היא, smell does not count.

phrases.english: Abaye says it is forbidden,
because smell is something real.
Rava says it is permitted,
because smell is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אָסוּר, רֵיחָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two rulings in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי holds smell is significant. רבא holds smell is insignificant.

steps.title: רבא's proof from bread baked with תרומה cumin
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves that smell is nothing from a משנה: bread baked in an oven heated with cumin of תרומה is permitted, because the bread only got the smell of the cumin, not its taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know that smell is nothing? From the משנה: if an oven was heated with cumin of תרומה and bread was baked in it, the bread is permitted, because it has no taste of cumin, only smell of cumin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to support his view that smell does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cumin of תרומה is forbidden to a non-כהן. The bread took on its smell, yet the משנה permits the bread. So a forbidden smell does not make something forbidden, which fits רבא's view.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it,
that smell is nothing at all?
As we learned: an oven that someone heated
with cumin of terumah
and baked bread in it:
the bread is permitted,
because there is no taste of cumin,
only the smell of cumin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reason from step 4 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that smell does not count (ריחא לאו מילתא היא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות: bread baked in an oven heated with תרומה cumin is permitted because it got only smell, not taste.

steps.title: אביי: there the forbidden thing was burned up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אביי would answer. He says the oven case is different, because the forbidden cumin was burned up, so the smell came from something no longer there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He would say it is different there, because the forbidden thing was burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אביי deals with רבא's proof, and answers that the משנה's case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the oven, the cumin was burned up before the bread got its smell, so the forbidden item no longer existed. With the wine barrel, the forbidden wine is still right there. So the משנה does not prove that smell from an existing forbidden item is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof from the cumin is pushed aside: אביי says a smell from something burned up is different from a smell from wine that is still there.

phrases.english: And Abaye? How would he explain this?
It is different there, because its forbidden item was burned up.
phrases.notes: He means the cumin was already destroyed by the fire. The wine in the barrel is still there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 5 by showing the case is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבא's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה the forbidden cumin was burned up, so its smell came from something no longer there. That is unlike wine still in the barrel.

steps.title: רב מרי ties the smell argument to an older argument about hot bread on a wine barrel
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says the argument between אביי and רבא matches an argument between תנאים. The case is hot bread placed on the opening of a barrel of תרומה wine: רבי מאיר forbids the bread, רבי יהודה permits it, and רבי יוסי splits between wheat and barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: This is like an argument of תנאים. Someone takes a hot loaf out of the oven and puts it on the opening of a barrel of תרומה wine. רבי מאיר forbids the bread, and רבי יהודה permits it. רבי יוסי permits wheat bread but forbids barley bread, because barley soaks up the smell. Isn't their argument exactly this: one holds smell is something real, and the other holds smell is nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings a משנה to show that the argument between אביי and רבא is really an older argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot bread soaks up the smell of the wine underneath it. If smell is something real, the bread now carries some of the תרומה wine and is forbidden to a non-כהן, which is רבי מאיר's view. If smell is nothing, the bread stays permitted, which is רבי יהודה's view. So רבי מאיר seems to match אביי, and רבי יהודה seems to match רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Like an argument between תנאים (the sages of the משנה)
One who takes bread out of the oven

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. רבי מאיר (forbids) lines up with אביי (smell is real). רבי יהודה (permits) lines up with רבא (smell is nothing).

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: It is like a dispute of Tannaim,
One who takes a hot loaf of bread out of the oven
and placed it on the opening of a barrel
of wine of terumah —
Rabbi Meir forbids the bread,
and Rabbi Yehuda permits it.
Rabbi Yosei permits it in the case of wheat bread,
and forbids it in the case of barley bread,
because barley draws in the smell.
Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds smell is something real,
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי מאיר, who forbids the bread.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: רֵיחָא וְלָא כְּלוּם הוּא?
phrases.english: and the other master holds smell is nothing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the oven proof and its rejection, the גמרא now shows that the whole argument already existed among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between אביי and רבא about smell matches the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about hot bread on a barrel of תרומה wine.

steps.title: Must אביי also accept that this is an argument of תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבא must accept that this is an argument of תנאים. It then asks whether אביי has to say that too, or whether he can read the משנה differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, it is certainly an argument of תנאים. According to אביי, must we say it is an argument of תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether אביי is forced to admit that a תנא, רבי יהודה, disagrees with him. This question sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says smell is nothing, so he agrees with רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר clearly forbids, so רבא has no choice but to admit that רבי מאיר disagrees with him. אביי, though, may be able to show that even רבי יהודה agrees smell is real, so that no תנא argues with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Must we say?

phrases.english: According to Rava, it is certainly a dispute of Tannaim,
but according to Abaye, must we say it is a dispute of Tannaim?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָבָא וַדַּאי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, לְאַבָּיֵי מִי לֵימָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests רב מרי's claim from אביי's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can אביי read the משנה so that רבי יהודה also holds smell is real?

steps.title: אביי begins his answer by quoting ריש לקיש on the case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers by quoting רבה בר בר חנה in the name of ריש לקיש, who explains the משנה case by case, starting with hot bread and an open barrel. The rest of ריש לקיש's statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can say to you: Wasn't it said about that משנה, that רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש: The case is hot bread and an open barrel...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to show that the משנה does not have to be an argument about whether smell is real. He does this by quoting ריש לקיש, who limits the case. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש starts with the case of hot bread and an open barrel, which is when the smell is strongest. By sorting the cases this way, אביי can show that רבי יהודה may also agree smell is real, and that the argument is only about other details. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense is coming)
It was stated about it (a later statement about the משנה)

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:
Was it not stated about that Mishnah,
that Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Reish Lakish said:
In the case of hot bread and an open barrel —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: לָאו מִי אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 8 from אביי's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה, based on an amora's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה permits because he holds smell is nothing, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still in progress. ריש לקיש's limit is the start of showing that רבי יהודה need not disagree with אביי.
